summary: The moderation and shared-tag authorization bypasses are fixed and deployed. Owner identity and immutable moderation metadata are enforced on creates, updates, replacement writes and deletes; trusted callable behavior was tested against local emulators. Public profile reads match the clarified product requirement. Storage now requires server-owned quota-backed permits. This is a rules assessment, not a guarantee of total website security.

findings.issue: Image record creation remains client-accessible without an aggregate Firestore record quota. Actual stored image objects require bounded server permits.
findings.recommendation: Move image record allocation behind the trusted upload allocator if stronger Firestore-cost controls are required.
